# THE CHECK NAMES BRANCH PROTECTION REQUIRES ON main.
#
# This file is a MIRROR of a setting that lives on GitHub, not the setting
# itself. It exists because the setting is invisible from inside the repository:
# nothing in .github/workflows records which job names are load-bearing, so a
# rename or a skip rule can remove a required check with no local signal at all.
#
# What that cost, on 2026-09-02: pull requests #650, #656 and #659 were all
# unmergeable at once, #659 with forty of forty checks green and nothing red
# anywhere. Three separate causes, none of them visible in a diff:
#
#   - `container: acceptance-docker` and `container: acceptance-multisource`
#     are deliberately not run on most pull requests, and a skipped job reports
#     nothing rather than success.
#   - `npm-audit` was split into a ui/web matrix, which renamed its checks to
#     `npm-audit (ui)` and `npm-audit (web)`; no check by the required name has
#     existed since.
#
# internal/testenv/required_checks_test.go asserts every name below is one some
# workflow job can actually emit. It cannot read the GitHub setting, so it
# cannot tell you this file has drifted from it -- it can only tell you the
# workflows stopped being able to satisfy what this file claims. That is the
# direction the failure came from all three times.
#
# WHEN YOU CHANGE BRANCH PROTECTION, CHANGE THIS FILE IN THE SAME COMMIT.
# Recover the live list with:
#   gh api repos/rainmanjam/polyemesis/branches/main/protection \
#     --jq '.required_status_checks.contexts[]' | sort
acceptance: acceptance
acceptance: acceptance-audio
acceptance: acceptance-encoders
acceptance: acceptance-failover
acceptance: acceptance-ladder
acceptance: acceptance-mqtt
acceptance: acceptance-playlist-phase0
acceptance: acceptance-postprod
acceptance: acceptance-pull
acceptance: acceptance-recording-stop
acceptance: acceptance-renditions
acceptance: acceptance-synth
acceptance: acceptance-tls
container: acceptance-browser
container: acceptance-docker
container: acceptance-multisource

which container suites

# SonarCloud analysis
#
# Added 2026-09-03, and it is the last item of the readiness audit's Stage 0.
# The job already FAILS on a red gate -- sonar-project.properties sets
# sonar.qualitygate.wait=true and internal/testenv/sonar_gate_test.go keeps it
# set -- but a failing job is not a blocked merge until the context is required
# here, which is a repository setting no test can commit. That gap is finding
# #648 in a different shape: a check that reports and cannot block leaves a wall
# of green that is not evidence.
#
# It earned the promotion the hard way. On PR #676 the gate failed for real --
# new_coverage 70.6% against a threshold of 80, every other condition clean --
# and nothing would have stopped that merge.
